I couldn't confirm this diagnosis. The retrieved snippets are only file-upload classes and e2e tests, and none of them contain the profile-update code. These candidates are inferred from the usual layout of this NestJS boilerplate, and the file paths and line ranges are estimates.

The most likely cause is that a profile update without a `photo` field writes `null` to the photo. A partial PATCH should leave the photo unchanged. The photo is only supposed to be cleared when the client explicitly sends `photo: null`.

candidates.explanation: Probable defect (unverified, since the code was not retrieved). The photo handling in update() likely turns an absent `photo` field into `null`. A PATCH that sends only `firstName` then overwrites the stored photo with null. An omitted photo should stay `undefined` so the existing value is kept. Only an explicit `photo: null` should clear it.

Second most likely (unverified). The repository merges the payload into the existing entity with `UserMapper.toPersistence({...UserMapper.toDomain(entity), ...payload})`. If the payload carries `photo: null` or `undefined` for the missing field, the spread overwrites the existing photo. The mapper may also drop the photo relation when it is not provided.

Third candidate (unverified). AuthService.update handles PATCH /auth/me and passes the DTO to UsersService.update. If it builds the update object with an explicit `photo` key, or a default of null, the photo is cleared whenever the client omits it.

fix.description: In UsersService.update, set `photo` to `undefined` by default. Resolve it through the file service only when `clonedPayload.photo?.id` is present, and set it to `null` only when `clonedPayload.photo === null` explicitly. Make sure the repository update skips undefined fields so the existing photo is preserved on partial updates.
